summary: Fábio Perini Airport (PBA) is a small regional airport serving the municipality of Cairu in Bahia, Brazil, located on Tinharé Island. It primarily functions as a gateway for tourists heading to Morro de São Paulo, one of Brazil's most celebrated beach destinations. The airport handles short-haul flights connecting the island to mainland cities such as Salvador.
faqs:
Q: What is Fábio Perini Airport used for?
A: The airport primarily serves tourists visiting Morro de São Paulo and the surrounding Tinharé Island beaches, offering a faster alternative to the longer ferry route from Salvador.

Q: Which airlines operate at PBA?
A: Small regional carriers and charter flights typically serve this airport, with connections mainly to Salvador da Bahia and other regional Brazilian destinations.

Q: Is the airport on Tinharé Island?
A: Yes, the airport is located on Tinharé Island, close to the town of Cairu and within reasonable distance of the Morro de São Paulo area.

Q: When is the best time to fly into PBA?
A: The airport operates during daylight hours, and flying in during the morning is recommended to allow time for onward connections to Morro de São Paulo by boat.
transport_tips: From the airport, travelers typically continue to Morro de São Paulo via a short boat or speedboat transfer, as vehicles are restricted on parts of the island. Shared vans and taxis can connect passengers from the terminal to nearby docks. Ferry services from São Joaquim terminal in Salvador remain an alternative if flights are unavailable or weather conditions affect operations.
local_tip: Pack light and bring only essentials in a backpack or soft bag—many transfer boats to Morro de São Paulo have tight space, and you'll be carrying luggage across sandy paths and up steps since most of the village is pedestrian-only with no vehicles allowed.
